title: Engineering and Characterization of an Optogenetic Model of the Human Neuromuscular Junction
protocol: Download a bioreactor CAD file from the Supplementary CAD File or create a custom design.
Generate a CNC toolpath from the 3D model using CAM software.
Machine acetal molds using a CNC milling machine.
Mix a 10:1 base to curing agent mixture of polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS, 77 g per mold).
Place the PDMS mixture into a vacuum chamber and close all valves.
Turn on the vacuum and de-gas the mixture for at least 30 min until no air bubbles remain.
Pour the PDMS mixture into molds and continue de-gassing in the vacuum chamber for 1 h.
Close the molds with the top half correctly oriented.
Place a steel hexagonal rod over the center of the closed mold and clamp on both sides.
Refill the top of the mold with PDMS.
Cure the molds in a 65 °C oven for at least 4 h.
Remove the platforms from the molds after cooling to room temperature.
Clean the devices in an ultrasonic bath using cycles of dish soap, isopropanol, and distilled water.
Dry the devices overnight at 65 °C.
Soak glass coverslips in 1% nonionic surfactant polyol for 30 min to ensure proper coating.
Rinse well with distilled water and dry the coverslips overnight at 65 °C.
Use a plasma cleaner on high with 6 L/min of oxygen for 1-2 min to treat glass coverslips and PDMS platform.
Press the PDMS down onto the treated coverslip for at least 30 s.
Autoclave the bonded devices before adding cells.
Attach a 573 nm dichroic mirror in the center of a 30 mm cage cube system.
Couple a red 627 nm LED with a 594 nm long-pass excitation filter to the top side of the cube, facing the mirror.
Attach a blue 488 nm LED with a 546 nm short-pass excitation filter to an adjacent side of the cube, facing the mirror.
Attach a ring-actuated iris diaphragm to the bottom of the cage cube to control the illuminated area size.
Power each LED by a T-Cube LED driver and control via an Arduino Uno Rev3 board.
Connect the side input of the LED driver to a power source plug.
Connect the middle output of the LED driver to the Arduino.
Connect the side output of the LED driver directly to the LEDs.
Connect the Arduino Uno to a PC via a USB cable.
Download files from GitHub.
Open the "Optical_Stimulation_Ramp_Arduino.ino" file from the GitHub folder.
Set starting parameters: Steps = 30; startFrequency = 0.5; endFrequency = 3; pulseLength = 100.
Ensure that pin output 4 is assigned to the Blue LED driver.
Assign pin output 2 to the Red LED driver.
Check that the middle wires of the LED driver are connected to ground and the respective pin output.
Compile and load the "Optical_Stimulation_Ramp_Arduino.ino" program to Arduino.
Connect each LED driver to its corresponding channel.
Thaw primary skeletal myoblasts (from Cook Myosite).
Expand thawed myoblasts using Myotonic growth medium (+ supplement) for up to six passages.
Maintain cells in an incubator at 37 °C and 5% CO2.
Change the media every 2 days.
When cells reach about 60% confluence, passage them with 0.05% Trypsin-EDTA (1x, for 5 min at 37 °C).
Collect dissociated cells and neutralize trypsin by adding fresh media.
Centrifuge the cell suspension at 300 x g and aspirate supernatant above the pellet.
Resuspend cells in MGM and seed them 1:3 with 60 mL per triple-layer flask.
Coat 6-well plates with 1 mL/well of solubilized basement membrane matrix diluted in DMEM/F12 (1:80).
Incubate the plates at room temperature for 1 h.
Seed iPSCs on coated 6-well plates with 2 mL of feeder-free cell culture medium.
Exchange 2 mL of media every other day.
Dissociate the stem cells by incubating with 1 mL of enzyme-free stem cell releasing reagent for 4 min.
Mechanically shear the cells with a wide tip P1000 pipette.
Seed cells at a ratio of 1:24 or 1:48 in iPSC media with 2 μM of Y-27632 dihydrochloride in 2 mL/well onto coated 6-well plates.
Isolate and count 30 x 10^6 myoblasts using an automated cell counter.
Resuspend the myoblasts in a 4:1 mix of 3 mg/mL collagen I and solubilized basement membrane matrix (800 μL of collagen mixture + 200 μL of basement membrane matrix to reach a final volume of 1 mL).
Add the accompanying neutralizing agent to the collagen component at a 9:1 ratio.
Dilute the collagen-neutralizing agent mixture with 1x PBS to achieve a volume of 800 μL.
Add 15 μL of cell-collagen suspension to each muscle chamber of the bioreactor, spreading the suspension across both pillars using the pipette tip.
Let the cell-gel mixture polymerize at 37 °C for 30 min.
Fill each bioreactor well with 450 μL of Myotonic growth media.
Begin myotube differentiation by switching tissues to 450 μL of fusion inducing media (FS) for 7 days, changing the media every other day.
Change the media to 450 μL of maturation media Ia (MMIa) on day 7.
Change the media to 450 μL of maturation media Ib (MMIb) on day 9.
Change the media to 450 μL of NbActiv4 on day 11.
Keep changing the media every 2 days until the motoneurons are seeded.
Transfer 4 x 10^6 ChR2-hiPSCs to an ultra-low attachment Petri dish with 15 mL of motoneuron suspension culture medium (MSCM).
Supplement MSCM with 3 μM CHIR99021, 0.2 μM LDN193189, 40 μM SB431542 hydrate, and 5 μM Y-27632 dihydrochloride.
Isolate the neurospheres (NS) with a 37 μM reversible strainer on day 2.
Replate isolated NS in 15 mL of MSCM supplemented with 3 μM CHIR99021, 0.2 μM LDN193189, 40 μM SB431542 hydrate, and 0.1 μM retinoic acid.
Transfer cells and media to a 50 mL tube on day 4.
Allow the neurospheres to settle for 5 minutes.
Aspirate the supernatant.
Resuspend the cells in 15 mL of MSCM supplemented with 0.5 μM SAG, 0.2 μM LDN193189, 40 μM SB431541, and 0.1 μM retinoic acid.
Repeat Step 6.3 but resuspend cells in 15 mL of MSCM supplemented with 0.5 μM SAG and 0.1 μM retinoic acid on day 7.
Repeat Step 6.3 but resuspend cells in 14 mL of MSCM supplemented with 10 μM DAPT on day 9.
Repeat Step 6.3 but resuspend the cells in 15 mL of MSCM supplemented with 20 ng/mL BDNF and 10 ng/mL GDNF on day 11.
Seed the motoneurons into the platform on day 14.
Prepare a 4:1 gel mixture of 2 mg/mL collagen I and Matrigel (800 μL of collagen mixture + 200 μL of Matrigel to reach a final volume of 1 mL).
Add the accompanying neutralizing agent in a 9:1 mix with the collagen component.
Dilute the collagen-neutralizing agent mixture with 1x PBS to achieve a final volume of 800 μL.
Use a 400 nm cell strainer to select large neurospheres and resuspend them in the gel mixture.
Aspirate media from the reservoir and carefully aspirate from the neurosphere well.
Add 15 μL of gel mixture into the neurosphere channel.
Load a 10 μL pipette with 10 μL of gel and pick one neurosphere.
Deposit the neurosphere into the neurosphere channel and ensure it is in the chamber.
Slowly raise the pipette while releasing the remaining gel once the neurosphere is deposited.
Check the location of the neurosphere using a microscope if unsure about its correct deposition.
Allow the gel to polymerize for 30 min at 37 °C.
Add 450 μL of NbActiv4 supplemented with 20 ng/mL BDNF and 10 ng/mL GDNF to the reservoirs.
Change the media every other day to allow axonal growth from neurospheres to muscle tissue.
Use a 2x objective on the microscope to image the microtissues.
Attach a live-cell chamber set at 37°C with 5% CO2 to the microscope stage.
Select the region of interest containing innervated skeletal tissues.
Place a 594 nm long-pass emission filter between the sample and the imaging objective.
Insert a rectangular 4-well plate containing 4 bioreactors (24 tissues) into the live-cell chamber.
Click Live View on the software interface to begin imaging.
Center and focus the image with the desired region of interest selected.
Upload custom macro code from GitHub to control stage position, Arduino board, and video acquisition.
Set output movie name as day_tissue group_tissue name_experiment.nd2.
Run the macro code with specified X,Y coordinates for stage positioning.
Acquire a fast time-lapse video with 1700 frames at 50 frames per second.
Replace the media after imaging is completed.
Return the samples to the incubator.
Allow at least 24 hours between image acquisition sessions to avoid tissue fatigue.
Prepare treatment media by adding external effector to NbActiv4 basal media supplemented with 20 ng/mL BDNF and 10 ng/mL GDNF.
For the MG sera experiment, use 20% MG patient sera in NbActiv4 + BDNF + GDNF.
For the BTX experiment, use 5 μg/mL BTX in NbActiv4 + BDNF + GDNF.
Stimulate/image using Step 3.2 to record baseline.
Replace media in tissues with treatment media (450 μL/tissue).
Incubate for the desired time (48 hours for patient sera, 20 minutes for BTX).
Stimulate or image again using Step 3.2 to record function after treatment.
Remove the treatment media.
Allow the tissues to rest for the desired time (48 hours after sera removal).
